text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and it does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatia signs air trafffic and cultural cooperation agreement with Ukraine as its Foreign Minister Genadiy Udovenko visits Zagreb.
- Presidential candidate and social democrat Zdravko Tomac says he offers a concept of a social democrtaic state which is now winning in Europe.
- Commentary: Will Croatia place a request for war reparations from Yugoslavia estimated at $22 billion?
- Liberal presidential candiadate Vlado Gotovac expects 25 percent of votes in the first round and a secure victory in the second one, he told a press conference.
- Dutch company NACO presented plans for a new airport terminal in Zagreb, worth $1.2 billlion, which should be completed by the year 2030.
- Oil concern INA may cut petrol prices and increase those for natural gas by five percent from July 1, government sources say.

- Government proposes a new law to protect small shareholders. Anyone wanting to buy a 25 percent company stake with voting rights would have to make a public offer equal to the highest share price recorded in the previous six months.
- Beginning of the tourist season brings jobs to 6,500 seasonal workers in hotels and restaurants along the Adriatic.
- International flower fair opens in Zagreb including exhibitors from Italy, Austria, Hungary, Columbia, Netherlands, Germany and the United States. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
